court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Vitthal Shriram Aghav And Others vs Rakhamabai Shriram Aghav And Another

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Vitthal Shriram Aghav, Subhadrabai Shriram Aghav, Ramesh Shriram Aghav, Nandkishor Vitthal Aghav, Yogesh Vitthal Aghav, Ratnamala D/o Vitthal Aghav, Rekha D/o Vitthal Aghav, Indubai W/o Shriram Aghav, Dnyaneshwar Sonaji Jadhav, Mahadu Mannu Shingane, Kaduji Bhikaji Jadhav
parties.respondent_defendant: Rakhamabai Shriram Aghav, Ushabai Pandharinath Nagare

facts_of_case: Deceased Shriram Chandrabhan Aghav married to Rakhamabai Shriram Aghav - Plaintiff No.1 and Subhadrabai Shriram Aghav - Defendant No.2. He was having issues out of these marriages.

legal_principles.principle: A judgment by a Subordinate Judge or a District Judge in exercise of the jurisdiction conferred upon them by the Hindu Marriage Act would surely fall within the purview of Sec. 41 of the Indian Evidence Act.
legal_principles.held: Any decision given in the exercise of matrimonial jurisdiction would be conclusive not only against the parties to the proceeding but against the whole world.
cited_cases: Bhagwan Dayal v. Reoti Devi, (1962) SC 287
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — applies to all matrimonial jurisdiction cases

legal_principles.principle: A judgment by a Court exercising matrimonial jurisdiction would operate as judgments in rem.
legal_principles.held: Such judgments would operate as judgments in rem.
cited_cases: Bhagwan Dayal v. Reoti Devi, (1962) SC 287
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — applies to all matrimonial jurisdiction cases
